description:
BGP route filtering troubleshooting scenario. An enterprise edge router is advertising all internal routes to an ISP peer instead of only the approved public prefixes. Diagnose why the configured prefix-list is not being applied and fix the route-map to properly filter outbound advertisements. Verify that only authorized prefixes are sent to the ISP while maintaining internal route propagation.

IP Addressing Plan:
- EDGE: eth1=203.0.113.2/30 (to ISP), eth2=10.1.0.1/30, eth3=10.2.0.1/30, lo=10.0.0.1/32
- ISP: eth1=203.0.113.1/30, lo=1.1.1.1/32
- INTERNAL1: eth1=10.1.0.2/30, lo=10.10.1.1/32
- INTERNAL2: eth1=10.2.0.2/30, lo=10.10.2.1/32

properties.description: Identify that ISP is receiving unwanted internal routes (10.0.0.0/8)
Diagnose that route-map exists but is not applied to BGP neighbor
Route-map FILTER-OUT now applied to ISP neighbor in outbound direction

evaluation.command: vtysh -c 'show ip bgp neighbors' | grep 'route-map out'

properties.description: ISP only receives authorized public prefix (203.0.113.0/30), not internal routes
ISP does not have internal routes (10.0.0.0/8) in BGP table

preconfiguration.command:
vtysh -c 'conf t
 ip prefix-list PL-PUBLIC-ONLY permit 203.0.113.0/30
 route-map FILTER-OUT permit 10
  match ip address prefix-list PL-PUBLIC-ONLY
 exit
 interface lo
  ip address 10.0.0.1/32
 exit
 interface eth1
  ip address 203.0.113.2/30
 exit
 interface eth2
  ip address 10.1.0.1/30
 exit
 interface eth3
  ip address 10.2.0.1/30
 exit
 router bgp 65000
  no bgp ebgp-requires-policy
  bgp router-id 10.0.0.1
  neighbor 203.0.113.1 remote-as 65001
  network 10.0.0.1/32
  network 10.1.0.0/30
  network 10.2.0.0/30
  network 203.0.113.0/30'

vtysh -c 'conf t
 interface lo
  ip address 1.1.1.1/32
 exit
 interface eth1
  ip address 203.0.113.1/30
 exit
 router bgp 65001
  no bgp ebgp-requires-policy
  bgp router-id 1.1.1.1
  neighbor 203.0.113.2 remote-as 65000
  network 1.1.1.1/32'

vtysh -c 'conf t
 interface eth1
  ip address 10.1.0.2/30
 exit
 interface lo
  ip address 10.10.1.1/32
 exit'

vtysh -c 'conf t
 interface eth1
  ip address 10.2.0.2/30
 exit
 interface lo
  ip address 10.10.2.1/32
 exit'

fault_verification.description: Verify that BGP session with ISP is established
Verify that ISP is receiving the internal route 10.0.0.1/32 (route leak)

optimal_solution.description: Check BGP neighbor config with 'show ip bgp neighbors', identify missing route-map application, review existing prefix-list and route-map with 'show route-map', apply route-map to neighbor with 'neighbor X.X.X.X route-map FILTER-OUT out', perform soft reset with 'clear ip bgp * soft out', verify filtering

research_context.citation: BGP troubleshooting scenarios and industry MTTR data. BGP route filtering is a critical enterprise skill covered in CCNP ENARSI and CCIE curricula. Industry MTTR for configuration errors: 15 minutes to 4 hours. BGP-specific issues can range from 30 minutes (simple config) to hours (complex policy debugging) based on Catchpoint BGP analysis and network engineering case studies.
research_context.literature_basis: BGP route filtering using prefix-lists and route-maps is a standard practice documented in RFC 4271 (BGP-4) and Cisco BGP best practices guides. This scenario represents a common operational error: having a filter policy defined but failing to apply it to the neighbor. This issue type is documented in multiple CCNP TSHOOT case studies and appears in real-world incident reports where misconfigurations led to route leaks (Network Defense Blog case studies, Moldstud network troubleshooting examples).
research_context.time_justification: 40 minutes represents realistic troubleshooting and verification time for BGP policy issues. Fast diagnosis (expert): 15-25min. Average resolution: 30-60min. Includes time for diagnosis using show commands, applying the fix, performing soft-reset, and verifying proper filtering from ISP perspective. Aligns with 15min-4hr MTTR range for configuration errors.
